analyst_view.overall: Besiktas (8th, 7 points) host Hapoel Be'er Sheva (33rd, 1 point) in Batumi, Georgia, because the game could not be staged safely in Istanbul; Hapoel's team manager says about 13,000 tickets have gone to Besiktas fans and around 16,000 are expected, so it should feel close to a home game, with heavy security and calls from Hapoel to avoid friction. Besiktas, coached by Vincenzo Italiano, trained in full on Tuesday and fly to Batumi on Wednesday after a 4-2 win at Konyaspor; no new injuries have been reported, and an earlier report had centre-back Umit Akdag serving the second game of a UEFA ban. Hapoel are without first-choice goalkeeper Ofir Marciano (torn calf, 2-3 weeks; Marco Wolf starts) and Lucas Ventura, while Eliel Peretz travels but is a big doubt; all of them are already in the numbers' missing list. Danish referee Morten Krogh averages few cards (2.9 a game), which the numbers already count. The news is small and points both ways, so I stay with the numbers on every stat.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.0 goals, about 2.3 for Besiktas and 0.7 for Hapoel, and already lift Besiktas for 15 goals in their last 6 (+4.1%) and for Marciano's absence in Hapoel's goal (+6.2%), with Wolf deputising. Akdag's reported ban weakens Besiktas' back line a little, but with a mostly Besiktas crowd in Batumi the home edge is largely kept. I stay at about 3.0.

corners.text: The numbers say 7.3 corners, 4.7 for Besiktas, already trimmed slightly for both sides' recent corner counts. Besiktas should have most of the ball against a side near the bottom of the table, and the neutral venue changes little for set pieces, so I stay at about 7.3.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.9 cards, with Hapoel the more booked side, and already take 12% off for referee Morten Krogh, who shows only 2.9 cards a game. The political tension around the fixture is real and security will be heavy, but with almost no Israeli away support and a mainly Besiktas crowd I see no clear push either way, so I stay at about 3.9.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.2 shots, 19.0 for Besiktas. With around 16,000 Turkish fans expected, losing the Istanbul crowd should cost little, and Besiktas' attack (Vlahovic, Trossard, Cerny) is scoring freely; the Galatasaray league game next could bring changes, but none are announced. I stay at about 27.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.5 on target, 7.8 for Besiktas, and already lift Besiktas for sharp recent finishing (+3.6%) and trim Hapoel's (-6.3%). A stand-in goalkeeper for Hapoel affects goals more than shots on target, and the venue change does not alter Besiktas' attack, so I stay at about 10.5.
